question: A 16-year-old boy presents to the emergency room with severe right shoulder pain following a painful overhead swing during a competitive volleyball match. On physical examination, the patient has limited active range of motion of the right shoulder and significant pain with passive motion. Suspecting a rotator cuff injury, the physician obtains an MRI, which indicates a minor tear in the tendon of the rotator cuff muscle that is innervated by the axillary nerve. Which of the following muscles was affected?

enhanced_information: The minor tear in the tendon of the rotator cuff muscle innervated by the axillary nerve indicates that the Infraspinatus muscle was affected. This conclusion is supported by the fact that the Infraspinatus muscle is treated by the ADRBK1 gene, which is associated with muscle structure. The evidence paths confirm the involvement of the axillary nerve and the role of the Infraspinatus muscle in this scenario.
analysis: The axillary nerve innervates the deltoid and teres minor muscles. Among the options provided, teres minor is the only muscle innervated by the axillary nerve. Therefore, the rotator cuff muscle affected in this scenario is the teres minor.
